content.text: In one sentence, prove there are infinitely many prime numbers.

content: If there were finitely many primes $p_1, \dots, p_n$, then $N = (p_1 \cdots p_n) + 1$ would leave a remainder of 1 when divided by any of them, meaning $N$ must have a prime factor not in the list (or be prime itself), which contradicts the assumption.

thoughts.subject: Formulating Prime Proof
thoughts.description: I'm working on crafting a concise one-sentence proof for the infinitude of primes. The challenge is distilling the standard proof down to its absolute essence, while maintaining rigor and clarity. Currently, I'm exploring variations on the contradiction argument involving the product of assumed primes. This requires careful phrasing to avoid ambiguity within the sentence's constraints.
